newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen dips by Tokyo noon, waiting for data.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen dips by Tokyo noon, waiting for data.

text.p: The key December Euroyen futures contract had dipped slightly by Tokyo midday but traders expected further losses to be limited, with selling pressure easing a bit prior to the release of Japanese industrial production data this afternoon.

"Key December briefly touched 98.75, but then recovered a bit, and this is likely to hold until the data comes out and maybe after that as well," one credit-bank trader said. Others agreed that the downside will be limited to 98.74 for now.
December ended the morning at 98.77 after moving from 98.75 to 98.79, with volume 46,893 contracts.
April industrial production figures, and forecasts for May and June, are due out at 0430 GMT.
The market is most closely watching the June forecast, although traders said no real consensus had been reached about what numbers are likely to emerge.
"If the June forecast is strong, December could try for 98.70. But the mood for sharp selling doesn't really seem to be there in the market just yet," a city bank trader said.
Interest rate swap levels were edging up, but at a slower pace than on Wednesday. The two-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.50/1.54 percent against 1.45/1.49 on Wednesday.

Key overnight call money was being traded at around 0.49 percent by midday, down from 0.52 percent on Wednesday, after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) performed its first accomodative money market operation since May 9, traders said.
The BOJ injected a net 100 billion yen into the market against a shortfall of 10 billion yen, as expected by the market.
In the longer end of the market, no certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued. Around 120 billion of three-month CDs were issued Wednesday at 0.60 percent.
